headline: CBA's cash NPAT rose 6% to $5,445 million in 1H26 (vs $5,132 million in 1H25). Statutory NPAT was $5,412 million. Total operating income grew 7% to $15,021 million, driven by NII volume growth of 8%, partly offset by a 4 bps margin decline. Operating performance increased 5% to $8,131 million. Underlying operating expenses rose 5% to $6,720 million, with $170 million in notable items. Loan impairment expense was flat at $319 million. Corporate tax expense increased $94 million to $2,367 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $761 million or 6% on the prior comparative period. The result was driven by a $96 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets, partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.04%. Margin drivers included asset pricing (-2 bps), funding costs (-3 bps), portfolio mix (+1 bps), and capital/replicating (+6 bps).

Other operating income increased $163 million or 8% to $2,326 million. Commissions rose $61 million to $1,146 million, lending fees increased $16 million to $465 million, trading income grew $84 million to $603 million, funds management income increased $7 million to $67 million, and other income decreased $5 million to $45 million.

Underlying operating expenses increased $348 million or 5% to $6,720 million. Staff expenses rose $169 million to $4,139 million, occupancy and equipment expenses increased $5 million to $465 million, information technology services expenses rose $134 million to $1,321 million, and other expenses increased $40 million to $795 million.
Restructuring and notable items were $170 million in 1H26, compared to nil in 1H25. These items are reported separately from underlying operating expenses.

Loan impairment expense was $319 million, a decrease of $1 million on the prior comparative period. This was driven by decreases in Business Banking ($129 million), Institutional Banking and Markets ($17 million), and New Zealand ($12 million), partially offset by an increase in Retail Banking Services ($153 million).

Corporate tax expense increased $94 million or 4% to $2,367 million, reflecting a 30.3% effective tax rate. The decrease in effective tax rate from 30.7% to 30.3% was primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses.

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items: $170 million (1H26) vs nil (1H25)
limitations: Capped at 80: operating_expenses -348 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
